Yes: several papers describe automated topic modeling built around clustering, including community-style graph clustering. TriTopic is an automated topic modeling framework that fuses embeddings, TF-IDF, and metadata in a graph and uses Consensus Leiden Clustering plus iterative refinement to produce stable topic partitions [2]. TopiCLEAR also does automated topic discovery by clustering embeddings with adaptive dimensionality reduction, with an emphasis on interpretable topics, especially for short texts [5].

If by “community clustering” you mean graph/community detection, the closest match is TriTopic’s graph-based topic modeling with Leiden clustering [2]. A related but not exactly topic-modeling paper organizes arguments into communities by building an interaction graph and applying community detection [7]. For hierarchical topic structure, EviMap and the density-tree method provide automated multi-level topic organization rather than flat clusters [9, 8].
